rv.q: Berry's production struggles some with the conversational reality of the domestic scenes, a crucial sharp contrast with the rehab sections.
Jonathan Berry’s moving production discovers new connections between story, artist and audience.
The play's brevity, which starts somewhat lethargically, picks up toward the end; however, it skips so much narrative needed to develop the characters that it loses its powerful meaning.
This sterling cast under the keen eye of Berry brings it all together and shows just how amazing 90 minutes of theater can be.

cn.t: Critics find this veteran's PTSD drama well-intentioned but uneven, with strong performances anchoring a story that resonates emotionally for some while leaving others wanting more depth in its exploration of trauma and recovery.
